name: Dash-Guti
region: Central Provinces, India (also United Provinces, Karwi Subdivision, where it is called Kowwu Dunki)
boardDescription: Lau Kata Kati 'butterfly' board (two triangles joined at a common vertex, 19 points) plus two short line segments attached to the common vertex, one on each side exterior to the triangles; 21 points total.
ruleNotes: Captures compulsory, by the short leap as in draughts/Alquerque, in a straight line following the board pattern; multiple captures per turn allowed. Win by capturing all enemy pieces. Stalemate loses; if no more captures are possible, the player with more pieces wins, equal counts draw. Each player's 10th piece starts on the antenna endpoint on that player's right-hand side (left end for the top player, right end for the bottom player).
sources: H.J.R. Murray, A History of Board-Games Other Than Chess (1952), p.70 (via Wikipedia 'Dash-guti' article)
